reports.title: Alabama Enacts 21st State Comprehensive Privacy Law (HB 351 — Alabama Personal Data Protection Act)
reports.summary: On April 7, 2026, the Alabama Legislature unanimously passed House Bill 351, the Alabama Personal Data Protection Act (APDPA), making Alabama the 21st state to enact a comprehensive consumer privacy law. The statute follows the Virginia-model framework but diverges in meaningful ways: no data protection impact assessment (DPIA) requirement, no universal opt-out/preference signal mandate, no private right of action, and a non-sunsetting 45-day cure period. Enforcement is exclusive to the Alabama Attorney General, with civil penalties capped at $15,000 per violation. The law takes effect May 1, 2027, pending the Governor's signature.
